newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi stocks close higher on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Delhi stocks close higher on foreign buying.

text.p: Delhi stocks closed higher on Tuesday, after a day of brisk buying, on short covering by foreign investors and speculators.
At the close of trading, the Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index ended 11.49 points higher at 909.28.
Traders said that India's largest mutual fund, the Unit Trust of India had started buying, after being a seller in the last several sessions.
"It seems that the market was in over-bought positions and might see some correction before staging another rally," Sanjay Mittal of stock broking firm S.R.M Securities said.
The leader of the pack was steel maker TISCO which rose 13.50 rupees to 204.50, on rumours of a hike in steel prices.
Cement companies performed strongly, brokers said, on expectations that cement demand would pick up shortly.
Associated Cement Companies Ltd rose 112.05 rupees to 1,543. Larsen & Toubro gained 12.55 rupees to 258.75.
The upward trend was visible in stocks of several multinational companies. Nestle India rose seven rupees to 295.
Smithkline Beecham Consumers Health climbed three rupees to 273.
Hindustan Lever dropped four rupees to 440, on profit-taking, brokers said.
State Bank of India gained 14 rupees to 354.85.
